Baugh, “The Mormons Must Be Treated as Enemies,” 292–93. Before attacks against Latter-day Saints in Missouri had intensified, First Presidency counselor Sidney Rigdon had spoken of a potential “war of extermination,” announcing his intention that Latter-day Saints would stand their ground. Rather than calling for the genocide of Missourians, his words acknowledged the impasse between the Saints and other Missourians. He and other Saints hoped for peaceful coexistence with their neighbors but refused to surrender to their opponents’ demands.
